laff.et: Borrowed from Low German laff, which is either inherited from Middle Low German *laf (seemingly not attested) or borrowed from Middle Dutch laf (early 15th century), all probably from Proto-Germanic *laba-, from Proto-Indo-European *leb- (“to hang loosely”). C…

s: Lafnitz (a tributary of the Rába, Austria and Hungary, flowing into the Danube)

Lafette.et: From Laffete, from L’Affuite (1665) and Affuiten (1617), from French l’affût (early 17tth century). Ultimately from Latin fūstis.

s: Ich lache ob den abgeschmackten Laffen, / Die mich anglotzen mit den Bocksgesichtern
›Dieser dumme Laffe, der Tscharski! Sie wollte ihn abweisen, das weiß ich sicher, verstand es aber nicht zu machen.‹
Laffe.et: Inherited from Middle High German laffen or laffe. Perhaps ultimately related to laff (“insipid, stale”).
